research_question: In people with first-episode or recent-onset psychosis, does adding cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) to standard care reduce negative symptoms of schizophrenia compared with standard care alone or another psychosocial intervention plus standard care?
treatment_label: CBT for psychosis added to standard care
control_label: Standard care alone or another psychosocial/active control intervention plus standard care
outcome_description: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia/psychosis measured with validated clinician- or self-rated instruments (e.g., PANSS negative subscale, SANS total, BPRS negative items, SNS, BNSS, NSA). One endpoint per study, preferring the medium-term assessment (post-treatment or follow-up at or before 12 months); if several eligible assessments exist, the one closest to 12 months and within 12 months is used. Continuous endpoint (post-treatment mean or change score) converted to a standardised mean difference.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g means the CBT-plus-standard-care group had a better outcome — i.e., lower/less severe negative symptoms (greater reduction on PANSS-negative, SANS, or equivalent) — than the control group.
search_queries: cognitive behavioural therapy first-episode psychosis randomised controlled trial negative symptoms
CBT early psychosis recent-onset schizophrenia trial symptom outcome
cognitive behaviour therapy psychosis PANSS negative SANS controlled comparison standard care
inclusion_criteria: Participants are people with first-episode, early, or recent-onset psychosis or schizophrenia-spectrum disorder (including at-risk/early intervention samples where psychosis onset is recent)

Study evaluates cognitive behavioural therapy (or a CBT-based/CBT-informed psychological intervention) delivered alongside standard care and compares it with standard care alone or another psychosocial intervention plus standard care
Reports some quantitative measure of negative symptoms (e.g., PANSS-negative, SANS, BPRS negative items) for both groups at any post-baseline assessment
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, protocol, qualitative or purely theoretical paper)
No comparison between a CBT/treatment condition and a control or comparison condition (e.g., single-arm or pre-post only design)
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means and SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios reported or derivable)
Completely unrelated to CBT and negative symptoms in psychosis (e.g., different population or purely pharmacological outcome with no negative-symptom data)
moderators_to_extract: Control condition type (treatment as usual vs. active psychosocial comparator)
Negative symptom instrument (PANSS-negative, SANS, BPRS, other)
Timing of endpoint (post-treatment vs. follow-up months since baseline)
Number of CBT sessions / treatment duration
Illness stage (first-episode vs. recent-onset/early psychosis vs. at-risk)
Risk of bias / blinding of outcome assessors
effect_size_note: Pool one continuous endpoint per study as a standardised mean difference (Hedges g), sign-oriented so that positive values favour CBT (lower negative-symptom severity). Where only change scores, t/F values, or medians/IQRs are available, convert using standard formulas.
